clue.text: The start of the alphabet rearranged by the French — what a fiasco!

indicators.note: rearranged tells us the opening run of the alphabet is to be put in a new order

parts.note: the alphabet starts A, B, C, D, E
le is the French masculine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone shuffling the ABC with a French twist ends up exclaiming at a complete shambles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The start of the alphabet' looks like the letter A alone; here it is the first five letters, which 'rearranged' turns into DEBAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A humiliating collapse or utter failure is both a fiasco and this word, which is borrowed from French.

clue.text: Hibernating animals need somewhere to sleep and something to eat

parts.note: a dorm, short for dormitory, is a shared sleeping room
an ice is an ice cream or sorbet

explanation.surface: Creatures preparing for winter need a bed and a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: These small rodents are famous for sleeping through the winter, like the one at the Mad Hatter's tea party.

clue.text: Large bird seen at the funfair

parts.note: large means big
a dipper is a small bird of fast streams

explanation.surface: A huge bird is spotted at the fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large bird' looks like a single thing to define; it is the wordplay, and the definition is the funfair ride.
explanation.definitionFit: This roller coaster, with steep dips, is a classic fairground ride; it is also a star pattern.

clue.text: Take round some fish, possibly

definitions.meaning: to take hold of, or seize
a round is a song for several voices entering in turn
the fish an angler lands in a day

explanation.surface: An instruction to carry some fish around.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: to seize, a part-song sung in canon, and an angler's haul.

clue.text: Just go, after objective finally accomplished

indicators.note: after puts the word for go behind the letter taken from objective
finally means we take only the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: to quit is to go or leave
an able person is skilled or accomplished

explanation.surface: Someone simply leaves once their goal has been reached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like an adverb meaning merely; it is the definition, meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair and impartial treatment is a synonym for being just.

clue.text: Champion's ahead in the game

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the word for the game

parts.note: a game can be called a sport
a team that is up is ahead in a match

explanation.surface: Someone's favourite contender is leading the match.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Champion stands for 'is', joining the verb-sense definition to the wordplay; 'Champion' reads as a noun on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause is to back it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Pay for a worthless horse

definitions.meaning: old British slang for wages or salary

explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a wage and an old term for a feeble nag happen to be the same word.

clue.text: European state leads in the last event

indicators.note: leads in means the state's abbreviation comes in front of the next piece

parts.note: a Pole is a person from Poland
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
ult., short for ultimo, means last month in old business letters

explanation.surface: A national from Europe is leading in the final competition.
explanation.walkthrough: ULT (ultimo) is an old commercial abbreviation for 'of last month'.
explanation.definitionFit: This athletic contest, leaping a bar with a long flexible pole, is a track and field event.

clue.text: At 'igher temperatures, aquatic creature…

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'At 'igher temperatures, aquatic creature…': the only parse is HOTTER with its H dropped, where 'igher both supplies part of the phrase meaning hotter and, by its apostrophe, signals the dropped H, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: … 'ad to get captured by t'rod

annotationWithheld.why: Clue '... 'ad to get captured by t'rod' has no definition of its own: its wordplay (AD inside T + POLE) covers every word, and the definition 'aquatic creature' sits in 7-down's clue, carried over by the dots

clue.text: Just satisfactory

definitions.meaning: satisfactory means acceptable or as it should be

explanation.definitionFit: Both a fair, correct outcome and an acceptable state of affairs are described by the same word.

clue.text: Not told outside the family.

definitions.meaning: read as ..., that is never narrated or recounted

explanation.definitionFit: A story never recounted and a stranger with no kinship share one word, from two senses of 'relate'.

clue.text: Left out in the cooking 'of Wiltshire's regional dish

indicators.note: cooking stirs the ingredients up, so the letters that remain are mixed into a new order
out tells us the abbreviation for left is taken away from the county name

parts.note: the English county name with its possessive s counted as a letter

explanation.surface: Something gets left out when a West Country cook prepares the local speciality.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing L from WILTSHIRES leaves WITSHIRES, which 'in the cooking' rearranges. Wiltshire is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: This mutton, potato and onion stew is a traditional dish of one particular country, Ireland.

clue.text: Group of stars scold a drop-out

indicators.note: read as 'drop out', telling us the letter a is removed

parts.note: a virago is a nagging, domineering woman, a scold

explanation.surface: A star gang rebukes someone who quit college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop-out' looks like a noun for a student who quits; here it means let the A drop out of VIRAGO.
explanation.definitionFit: This zodiac constellation, the Virgin, is a named pattern in the night sky.

clue.text: Hungry? Some food may tempt you to…

indicators.note: some tells us only a part of the following words is used, the run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A tempting snack is dangled before someone with an appetite, the sentence trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'tEMPT You'. The dots lead on to 15 across, whose clue continues the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose stomach is hollow and unfed feels this way, an informal synonym.

clue.text: A sailor may snatch a few breaks

indicators.note: breaks means the letters are broken up and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A busy seafarer might grab a short rest now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of MAY SNATCH are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sails a pleasure boat is a kind of sailor.

clue.text: … feast — heartlessly take a seat

parts.note: a banquet is a grand feast

indicators.note: heartlessly tells us the middle of the next word is removed, keeping only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Continuing 13 across: after the feast, someone is coldly told to sit down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' removes AK from 'take'. The dots carry the sentence on from 13 across, which ends 'Some food may tempt you to…'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an upholstered bench along a wall, as in a restaurant, a type of seating.

clue.text: Want to be observed turning up without eats

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the reversed piece goes around the other
in a down clue turning up means the word reads from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: seen means observed
dines means eats

explanation.surface: Someone longs to be noticed going hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' makes NEES, which goes around DINES. 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Poverty or lack, as in a state of want, is a synonym.

clue.text: Sent pictures via the Tube

parts.note: the Tube looks like the London Underground, but it is slang for the television set; pictures sent through it were broadcast

explanation.walkthrough: 'the Tube' suggests the London Underground railway; it is the cathode-ray tube of an old television, the 'box'.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcast on the small screen is the meaning, transmitting images to viewers.

clue.text: "Repeal act!" bursts out the advocate

indicators.note: bursting out scatters the letters of the quoted phrase into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A protester shouts a demand that a law be repealed.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of REPEAL ACT are rearranged. In Christian theology the Holy Spirit is called the Comforter or Advocate.
explanation.definitionFit: This Greek-derived title for the Holy Spirit means one who pleads on another's behalf, as in John's gospel.

clue.text: Margaret, up country, has a second fabulous horse

parts.note: Peg is a pet form of the name Margaret

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the country's letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: A woman called Margaret, travelling up through the country, owns a second legendary steed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns US into SU in this down clue; 'has' is a link, and the pieces A and S slot either side of it.
explanation.definitionFit: This winged steed of Greek myth is a creature of legend, the sense of fabulous here.

clue.text: What makes canon gorge?

parts.note: a small wavy mark over the n turns the word canon into the Spanish-style spelling for a deep ravine

explanation.walkthrough: 'canon' looks like a church rule or a big gun; with a mark over its n it becomes cañon, a canyon, which is a gorge.
explanation.definitionFit: This wavy diacritic, written over n in Spanish, changes the sound and so the word's meaning.

clue.text: Being an ascetic, catching cold

indicators.note: catching means the first word holds the other inside it

parts.note: the Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect of Roman times
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Living as a hermit, someone comes down with a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' looks like a verb; here it is the noun meaning existence or innermost nature.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing's fundamental nature or existence is a philosophical synonym for its being.

clue.text: What a gardener has to do is hard work

definitions.text: What a gardener has to do
definitions.meaning: joining a shoot onto a rootstock is a gardener's job
British slang for toil or hard labour

explanation.surface: A gardener's tasks are described as tough labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Splicing a cutting onto another plant and slogging away share one word, the second a British informal sense.

clue.text: Couple in trouble when tax year starts

indicators.note: in tells us the couple's abbreviation goes inside the word for trouble

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
PR is the abbreviation for pair, a couple

explanation.surface: A pair get into difficulty at the start of the financial year.
explanation.walkthrough: The UK tax year begins on 6 April.
explanation.definitionFit: The British fiscal year begins in this spring month, a piece of general knowledge.

clue.text: Where I was going, in rhyme, isn't as I've represented

definitions.text: Where I was going, in rhyme

indicators.note: represented is read as re-presented, the letters shown again in another order

explanation.surface: Someone insists their own account of where they were heading has been misrepresented.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ISN'T AS I'VE are rearranged. The nursery rhyme begins 'As I was going to St Ives, I met a man with seven wives'; St Ives is a town in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional riddle-rhyme names this Cornish town as the narrator's destination, a literary allusion.

clue.text: Pale bit of meat, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word for a bit of meat is spoken and a different spelling entered

parts.note: a steak is a thick slice of beef

explanation.surface: A pallid slice of meat, by the sound of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pale' looks like an adjective meaning pallid; it is the noun for a fence post.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale is a pointed wooden post for a fence, as in 'beyond the pale'.

clue.text: Path from river in shadow

indicators.note: in tells us the river abbreviation goes inside the word for shadow

parts.note: to shadow someone is to tail them

explanation.surface: A track leads away from a river into the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shadow' looks like a noun for shade; it is the verb meaning follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A track through countryside is a synonym for a path.

clue.text: Fabric may get loose ends and fray

parts.note: scrim is a light open-weave cotton or linen fabric

indicators.note: loose ends tells us each of the two words lets go of its last letter

explanation.surface: Cloth with loose threads starts to unravel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may' loses Y and 'get' loses T, leaving MA and GE after SCRIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A confused scuffle or tussle is a fray, a synonym for a disorderly fight.

clue.text: Crime for which clerk was guillotined

indicators.note: a guillotine takes off the head, so the first letter of the word for clerk is removed

parts.note: a clergyman, legally a clerk in holy orders, is a parish priest or vicar

explanation.surface: An offence for which a clerk was beheaded during a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: The clergy were formally 'clerks in holy orders', so a clerk can be a parson; 'guillotined' cuts off its head, P.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Gag the rest, according to Hamlet

definitions.meaning: to gag someone is to stop them speaking
Hamlet's dying words are 'The rest is' followed by this word

explanation.surface: A line from Hamlet is quoted as a reason to shut someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: To muzzle someone, and Hamlet's final word for what follows death, are the same word.

clue.text: Leaders of school parties stop in this spot

indicators.note: leaders of means we take the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: to lodge is to stop or stay in a place

explanation.surface: Head pupils of school groups stay over at this location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spot' looks like a place, but it is the definition as a blob or stain.
explanation.definitionFit: A blot, smear or large stain is an informal synonym for a mark like this.
